model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral mixin for typed dependency and downstream impact. This bounded pass covers the impact-scenario half only: how a change, event or hypothetical stress condition is framed as a scenario input, how effect is assumed to propagate over separately declared dependency assertions, which entities end up in the affected set with which status, and with what traceability, uncertainty and claim status the result may be published.
model.scope_statement: In scope is the semantics of an impact scenario evaluated against a cited dependency-graph snapshot: trigger inputs, scenario identity and version, counterfactual baseline, analysis mode and time horizon, propagation assumptions, traced paths and excluded edges, affected-set membership with explicit negative/unknown/conditional/non-propagating statuses, effect characterisation, outcome uncertainty and limitation disclosure. Out of scope is the typed dependency assertion itself (the adjacent split area of this same model), and every decision or action that an impact result may inform: approval, authorisation, scheduling, execution, rollback, notification, remediation, enforcement and audit-trail storage. The model is a mixin: it attaches impact-scenario semantics to whatever entities an adopting Dimension already registers, and never becomes the master record for those entities.
in_scope: Trigger inputs typed as proposed change, occurred event, hypothetical stress condition or standing condition, carried by reference to their owning model
Scenario identity, version, declared assumptions and the cited dependency-graph snapshot against which the scenario was evaluated
Counterfactual baseline: the state or projected evolution without the trigger, and whether effect is expressed as a delta or an absolute end state
Analysis mode (prospective analysis, retrospective observation, reconciliation) and the separation of analysis time, trigger time, effect time and observation time
Effect horizon, short/medium/long-term banding, permanence and reversion time
Propagation assumptions: propagating and non-propagating edge types, traversal direction, depth and stop conditions, conditional predicates, cycle and redundancy handling
Affected-set membership with explicit per-entity status including not-affected, unknown/under-investigation, conditional and reached-but-not-propagating, each with justification
Effect characterisation: kind, polarity including neutral and beneficial, magnitude on a referenced scale, first-order versus downstream ordering, declared accumulation with other scenarios
Traceable path from trigger to each affected member, excluded edges with reason codes, and a traversal completeness code
Outcome uncertainty, likelihood and confidence qualifiers, claim status separating exposure inference from attributed cause, and mandatory limitation disclosure
out_of_scope: Definition, typing, criticality, versioning or retraction of dependency edges and graph snapshots - the adjacent split area of WM-XCT-037, consumed here only by reference
Approval, authorisation, scheduling, implementation, freeze windows and rollback of changes - owned by a change or release model
Incident detection, escalation, resolution and post-incident review lifecycle - owned by an event or incident model
Risk appetite, tolerance, acceptance and control selection - an impact result is an input to risk determination, not a risk decision
Stakeholder notification, recipient selection, issuing notices and acknowledgement tracking
Runtime evaluation engines, enforcement of policy, blocking of deployments and any execution semantics
Audit-trail capture, storage, tamper-evidence, retention and replay - this model emits audit payloads and consumes a referenced audit model
Identity, ownership, registration and decommissioning of the entities that appear in an affected set - owned by an asset or configuration-item registry
Definition of severity scales, units and conversions - referenced from a measurement model
Formal causal identification methods, cascading-failure simulation, monetary valuation and cost-benefit analysis

boundary_notes.neighbor: Dependency-assertion structure of WM-XCT-037 (adjacent split area of the same model)
boundary_notes.distinction: That area answers what depends on what, of which type, in which direction and with what criticality, and owns edge lifecycle. This area answers what a given trigger reaches across those edges, with what effect and with what confidence. An impact scenario consumes a cited, immutable graph snapshot; it never creates, retypes, retracts or repairs an edge, and a data-quality objection raised here is a finding against the graph owner rather than a local edit.

This model describes consequences and never approves, authorises, schedules, implements or rolls back anything. Severity in an impact result confers no mandate; the change model owns the decision, its authority and its execution record. The trigger is carried as a resolvable reference plus impact-specific seed parameters only.

Level of impact and likelihood of occurrence are produced here as analytical outputs that a risk determination may consume. Risk appetite, tolerance thresholds, acceptance, residual-risk tracking and control selection are not modelled here, and no impact record may be read as a risk acceptance.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Provenance model aligned to W3C PROV
boundary_notes.distinction: PROV records that one entity or activity influenced another and deliberately stops short of causation or effect magnitude. This model shapes its derivation records to PROV Entity/Activity/Agent with qualified derivation, and adds polarity, magnitude, horizon and claim status on top. It does not redefine PROV terms, and prov:wasInfluencedBy must never be read as a causal claim produced by this model.

VEX answers exploitability of one vulnerability in one product and CSAF owns advisory document lifecycle, product trees, remediations and distribution. This model generalises the affected-status vocabulary and the requirement to justify a not-affected determination to arbitrary triggers, but publishes no advisories and issues no remediation guidance.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Statutory impact assessment procedures (EU environmental impact assessment, Better Regulation impact assessment)
boundary_notes.distinction: Those instruments prescribe legal procedure, consultation, competent authority and decision competence. This model borrows only their analytical vocabulary - baseline scenario and likely evolution without the project, direct/indirect/secondary/cumulative effects, short/medium/long-term and permanent/temporary effects, and disclosure of forecasting methods, difficulties and main uncertainties - without claiming conformance with or authority under any of them.

Retrospective outcome records carry an observation time distinct from event time, but signal collection, thresholds, alerting and monitor health are owned by a monitoring model. Binding an observation to a scenario is optional and asserts co-reference, not causation.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Audit trail and evidence record model
boundary_notes.distinction: This model specifies which state transitions must be emitted as audit events and with which fields. It does not own audit capture, ordering, tamper-evidence, retention or replay, and holding an impact record never grants access to or authority over an audit trail.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the Entity/Activity/Agent core, the qualification pattern (qualifiedDerivation, qualifiedInfluence, Influence), wasDerivedFrom and the deliberately weak wasInfluencedBy, plus startedAtTime, endedAtTime and generatedAtTime. Grounds derivation of an impact result from scenario inputs and the explicit rule that influence is not a causal claim.

sources.title: Directive 2011/92/EU on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (consolidated text, as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU)
sources.relevance: Annex IV point 3 requires a baseline scenario and the likely evolution without implementation; point 2 requires reasonable alternatives; point 5 requires direct effects and any indirect, secondary, cumulative, transboundary, short-, medium- and long-term, permanent and temporary, positive and negative effects; point 6 requires the forecasting methods used plus details of difficulties encountered and the main uncertainties. This is the strongest primary anchor for baseline, effect typing, horizon and completeness disclosure.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-30 Revision 1: Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
sources.relevance: Defines a generic risk model separating threat source, threat event, vulnerability, predisposing condition, likelihood of occurrence and level of impact, and requires assessments to document scope, assumptions, constraints and the confidence and uncertainty in results. Grounds the separation of trigger from effect, the impact-oriented analysis approach, and mandatory assumption and uncertainty disclosure.

sources.title: Minimum Requirements for Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VEX)
sources.organization: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), U.S. Department of Homeland Security
sources.relevance: Establishes that a negative determination is a first-class published statement: the four statuses (not affected, affected, fixed, under investigation), the requirement that a not_affected status carry a justification such as vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path or otherwise an impact_statement, and minimum metadata for author and role, timestamp, version and product identification including subcomponents and dependencies. Grounds explicit negative, unknown and non-propagating results.

sources.title: Common Security Advisory Framework Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Provides typed product relationships (default_component_of, installed_on, installed_with, optional_component_of) referenced by product_reference and relates_to_product_reference, product_status values, VEX flags and justifications, and document tracking with id, version, status, initial_release_date, current_release_date and revision history. Grounds edge-type selection for propagation, status vocabulary and versioned result records.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)
sources.relevance: Requires business impact analysis of exposures to severe business disruptions using quantitative and qualitative criteria and scenario analysis, testing against severe but plausible scenarios, a register of information on ICT third-party contractual arrangements, and assessment of concentration risk. Grounds scenario-based impact analysis over a maintained dependency register, and the separation of that register from the analysis performed on it.

sources.title: IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures
sources.organization: International Sustainability Standards Board, IFRS Foundation
sources.version_or_date: Issued June 2023; effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024
sources.relevance: Requires disclosure of effects over the short, medium and long term and the use of scenario analysis to assess resilience, with the inputs, assumptions and method of that analysis disclosed. Used analogically to ground horizon banding as a Dimension-declared parameter and scenario assumptions as disclosable inputs, not as a sector obligation.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Requires every time value to carry a stated offset to UTC, defines Z as equivalent to +00:00, specifies the time-second element including leap seconds, and reserves -00:00 for the case where UTC is known but the local offset is not. Grounds the timestamp rule and the refusal to default a missing offset.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.relevance: Supplies TemporalEntity, Instant, Interval and ProperInterval, hasBeginning, hasEnd and hasTemporalDuration, TemporalPosition and the thirteen Allen interval relations. Offered as an optional alignment for expressing effect horizons and the ordering of trigger, effect and observation intervals without prescribing a serialisation.

sources.title: Better Regulation Guidelines and Toolbox
sources.version_or_date: Better Regulation Guidelines of 3 November 2021; Better Regulation Toolbox version of 1 December 2025
sources.relevance: Sets out the European Commission impact assessment method in which options are compared against a defined baseline scenario, direct and indirect impacts are identified, analysis is proportionate to significance, and assumptions and uncertainty are made explicit. Corroborates the baseline and completeness requirements independently of the environmental impact assessment regime.

sources.title: Guidelines for Human Exposure Assessment
sources.relevance: Establishes exposure as contact or connection, formally distinct from dose and from adverse effect, organises assessment around explicit exposure scenarios, and requires variability and uncertainty to be characterised and confidence communicated. Grounds the separation of dependency-based exposure from assessed effect and from attributed cause.

bundles.name: Impact scenario framing and propagation inputs
bundles.description: Everything that must be fixed before an impact result can exist: what is being analysed, as which versioned scenario, against which baseline, in which analysis mode and over which horizon, and under which propagation assumptions. All of it is input-side and none of it asserts an outcome.
bundles.rationale: Impact statements are only falsifiable if their inputs are separable and citable. Statutory impact assessment requires a described baseline and its likely evolution without the project, described alternatives, and a stated forecasting method before effects may be reported; scenario-based business impact analysis requires severe but plausible scenarios to be declared. Grouping trigger, scenario, baseline, frame and propagation assumptions in one bundle keeps them versionable and reviewable independently of results, and keeps the dependency graph itself firmly outside as a cited input.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Analysis mode, the four separated time values, horizon bands, permanence and scope bounds are typed scalar fields of the scenario and result headers, not separately produced deliverables. Promoting them to their own artifact would create a second place where the analysis timeline can drift from the scenario specification and the trace record that already carry them, and would invite a mode or horizon to be revised without a corresponding scenario version. The substantive documents that carry these values are the scenario specification and the impact trace record, both declared in adjacent findings; interval and Allen-relation expression is an optional external alignment rather than a locally stored object.

bundles.name: Impact results, traceability and epistemic status
bundles.description: The output side: which entities the scenario reaches and with what explicitly recorded status, how each effect is characterised, which paths and exclusions produced the result, and what claim status, uncertainty and limitations must accompany it before it may be published or consumed.
bundles.rationale: A result is only usable if a reviewer can reconstruct it and if the reader can tell what kind of statement it is. Vulnerability exchange practice establishes that a negative determination is a first-class published statement carrying a justification, not an omission. Risk assessment guidance requires assumptions, constraints and confidence to be documented alongside results, statutory impact assessment requires disclosure of forecasting methods, difficulties and main uncertainties, and exposure assessment practice keeps exposure formally distinct from effect. Grouping results with their traceability and epistemic qualification prevents an exposure inference from being read as a causal finding or an authorisation.

layers.name: Affected set and effect characterisation

findings.name: Affected-set membership and per-entity status

Absence from the set never means 'not affected'; negative, unknown and conditional determinations are published as members so that a shorter set cannot masquerade as a smaller impact.

Level of impact and likelihood produced here can feed a risk determination that separates threat source, threat event, vulnerability and predisposing condition. Risk appetite, tolerance thresholds, acceptance, residual-risk tracking and control selection are not modelled here, and no impact record constitutes a risk decision.

Shape the scenario, the traversal run and the result as PROV Entity, Activity and Agent with qualified derivation, so that a result's dependence on its inputs is expressible in a standard vocabulary. canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the abstract record, not any serialisation: an ordered scenario header, an unordered set of affected-set entries keyed by entity reference, an ordered path list per entry, and an unordered exclusion set. Projection to JSON, YAML, Markdown, RDF, a document store, a graph store, a Git tree or an MCP-served resource changes nothing about meaning.

Before hashing or comparison, sort affected-set entries by entity identifier, paths by their edge-reference sequence, and exclusions by edge identifier, so that two projections of one result hash identically.

All time values canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. A value lacking an offset is invalid and is rejected rather than defaulted to local time or UTC; -00:00 is preserved with its distinct meaning of known UTC and unknown local offset.
An absent entry is never canonically equivalent to a not-affected entry. Canonicalisation must never drop, merge or elide a member, an exclusion or a path in order to shorten a result.

Code values canonicalise as a code-list identifier, code-list version and code triple. A consumer encountering an unrecognised code canonicalises it to unknown, never to not-affected or to a default severity.

Narrative fields canonicalise with normalised line endings and trimmed trailing whitespace only; no summarisation, truncation or reflow is permitted, because limitation disclosures lose meaning when shortened.
patch_rules: A released scenario, result, trace or disclosure version is immutable. Any change to trigger, baseline, snapshot, propagation profile, horizon or code-list binding produces a superseding version with an explicit supersession link and a change reason, never an in-place edit.
Patches to a draft are additive wherever possible. Removing an affected-set entry from a draft requires an exclusion reason code so that the negative or unknown result survives the edit.
A retrospective observation never patches a prospective result. The two are related only through a separate reconciliation record that leaves both sources untouched.
A correction to a released disclosure is issued as an erratum version citing the corrected version; the original is retained so that decisions made on it remain explicable.
A status change on an affected-set member is a patch that appends a new determination with its time, assessor and justification; it never overwrites the previous determination.
Re-derivation after a graph snapshot changes always produces a new result version; an existing trace record is never rewritten to match a newer snapshot.
compatibility_rules: Adding a status, justification, exclusion-reason or claim-status code is a minor change only where consumers are contractually required to treat unrecognised codes as unknown. Absent that guarantee it is breaking.

Changing the meaning of an existing status, reversing traversal-direction semantics, or altering the declared basis for calling an effect direct rather than indirect is a major, breaking change and requires dependent results to be re-issued rather than reinterpreted.
Removing or making optional any of claim status, traversal completeness, exclusion reasons or the limitation disclosure is always breaking, because each is a condition of safe consumption.

External alignments to PROV, OWL-Time, CSAF, VEX and RFC 3339 are versioned bindings. An upstream version change is recorded as a new binding with a conflict note where semantics moved; it is never applied as a silent reinterpretation of existing records.
A projection change - for example moving from files in version control to a document store or an MCP interface - is never a compatibility event, because the canonical form is projection-neutral.

identity_priority: The authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the artifact - for example the assessment, scenario, trace or disclosure identifier minted by the adopting Dimension's impact-assessment system of record. This is always preferred where it exists.

A governed global identifier or IRI from a registry the Dimension has bound - for example a CVE identifier for a vulnerability trigger, or a CSAF document tracking identifier for an advisory-sourced trigger - used only where no master-system identifier exists.
A UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only where neither of the above exists, and then published so that it becomes resolvable within the Dimension's namespace.
A date, a timestamp, a version label, a scenario or artifact title, a status value or a severity value is never an identifier and must not be used as one, alone or in combination.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every time value is recorded as an RFC 3339 date-time including seconds and an explicit numeric offset or the Z designator; a local time without an offset is rejected rather than defaulted, and -00:00 is used only in its RFC 3339 sense of UTC known with local offset unknown. Event time - when the trigger occurred or is scheduled to occur, and when an effect began - is recorded in fields separate from observation or ingestion time, which is when an assessor observed the outcome or the receiving system accepted the value, and separate again from analysis time, which is when the assessment was computed, and from baseline observation time. A record must never collapse these into one field, a prospective effect time must never be back-filled from an ingestion timestamp, and where only one of them is known the others are recorded as absent rather than copied.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts - scenario specification, baseline statement, propagation profile, affected-set register, trace record and disclosure - are named <artifact-type>/<stable-artifact-id>/<version>, where the version is a monotonic integer or semantic version that never encodes a date, never restarts and never carries status or severity. The stable artifact id is constant across every version; supersession, erratum and withdrawal are expressed by explicit links and status codes, never by reusing or colliding a name. A result, its trace record and its disclosure share a release group so that the three versions released together can be cited as one set.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each released artifact records a content hash over its canonical form together with the identifiers, versions and hashes of every input it cites: trigger record, graph snapshot, baseline statement, propagation profile and each bound code list, plus the accountable assessor. A result whose cited snapshot, profile or code-list version cannot be resolved is marked unverifiable and is never silently re-derived; re-derivation always produces a new version with its own citations. Redactions retain a hash of the pre-redaction canonical form so that suppression is detectable without exposing content. Signature formats, key management, attestation storage and audit-trail persistence are consumed from the referenced audit and security models and are not implemented, retained or replayed here.

policies: No impact record, at any severity, constitutes an approval, authorisation, instruction, notification, remediation or enforcement. Every released result carries an explicit non-authorisation statement naming the change, risk and notification models that own those decisions, and no projection may strip it.

Negative, unknown, conditional and non-propagating results are first-class and must be published as members with justifications, never suppressed by omission. A shorter affected set is not evidence of a smaller impact, and any filtered read must report the counts it suppressed.

Every asserted outcome carries a claim status. Dependency reachability alone may only be published as an exposure inference; an attributed-cause claim requires cited evidence meeting the Dimension's declared minimum, and is otherwise automatically downgraded.

Every result cites exactly one dependency-graph snapshot version, one propagation profile version and one set of code-list versions. Results mixing snapshots, or derived from an unrecorded snapshot, must not be released.

A completeness code and a limitation and uncertainty disclosure - covering forecasting method, difficulties encountered, data deficiencies, unmodelled mechanisms and main uncertainties - are mandatory sections of any released result.

This model never writes to the dependency graph, the trigger record, the entity registry or the audit trail. It reads them by citation and emits payloads; all persistence and enforcement in those systems belongs to their owners.

read: Read a scenario, its inputs, its result set, trace and disclosure by identifier and version. Reads are always version-pinned; resolving to an implicit latest is prohibited because a decision must be attributable to the exact record that informed it.

Read the affected set filtered by status, but a filtered read must return the counts it suppressed by status so that negative, unknown and conditional members remain visible as counts even when their detail is withheld.

Resolve a recorded path by dereferencing edge references into the dependency-assertion area. Where an edge no longer resolves, return the recorded historical path plus an unresolved-edge marker rather than re-deriving the path against a newer snapshot.
A result may not be served without its claim status, traversal completeness code and limitation disclosure; a projection that omits any of them is a non-conforming read.
create: Create a scenario only with a resolvable or explicitly unresolvable trigger reference, at least one seed entity, a declared baseline kind including the value none-declared, a cited graph snapshot with time and hash, and a cited propagation profile version.
Create a result only as a derivation of exactly one scenario version, capturing analysis time separately from trigger time, effect time and observation time, and recording the accountable assessor.
Create a retrospective observation independently of any scenario. Binding it to a scenario is optional, is marked as co-reference and never asserts causation.
Create a reconciliation record only where both the prospective result version and the observation records are cited with explicit versions, times and a stated comparison window.
update: Drafts of scenarios, results, traces and disclosures may be updated in place until release; release freezes the version and makes it immutable.
Released records are updated only by issuing a superseding version that links to its predecessor and states which specific input changed; the predecessor is retained unaltered.

A status change on an affected-set member appends a new determination with justification, assessor and determination time; prior determinations are retained so that the history of a negative or unknown finding is reconstructable.
Bound code lists and external alignment versions are updated by recording a new binding with a conflict note; existing records keep the binding versions under which they were produced.
delete: This model deletes nothing by default. Released scenarios, results, traces and disclosures reach their end state through supersession, withdrawal or tombstoning. A tombstone retains the stable identifier, version, artifact type, supersession or withdrawal link and the reason, and removes only the withdrawn payload, so that a decision taken on the record remains explicable.

Retention periods, legal hold and disposition schedules are set and executed by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy owner and, where the trigger is a regulated change or incident, by the model that owns that trigger. This model defines no retention period and performs no destruction; deletion execution is outside its boundary.

When an upstream registry deletes, merges or anonymises a referenced entity, the affected-set entry is marked reference-unresolvable and retained. Cascading deletion from a registry into impact records is prohibited, because it would silently rewrite historical assessments and remove evidence of what was known at analysis time.

Where personal data appears in a narrative field, an erasure request is supported by redaction in place with a redaction marker, the redacting role and time, and a retained hash of the pre-redaction canonical form. This model records the request and applies the redaction to its own payload; adjudicating the request, and executing erasure in referenced systems, belong to the Dimension's privacy and retention policy owners.

Deletion, withdrawal and redaction actions are emitted as audit payloads to the referenced audit model. This model does not own audit capture, retention, immutability or replay, and holding an impact record confers no authority over an audit trail.

roles.name: Impact model steward
responsibilities: Maintain the scenario, profile, status, justification, exclusion-reason and claim-status vocabularies and their versions
Approve major and breaking changes and enforce the compatibility rules
Keep AGENTS.md, the bound code-list list and the alignment binding versions current
Arbitrate boundary questions with the dependency-assertion owner and refuse structure that would import edge, approval, notification, enforcement or audit semantics

roles.name: Scenario author
responsibilities: Frame the trigger reference, seed entities, baseline, analysis mode, horizon and scope
Cite the graph snapshot and propagation profile versions and declare all assumptions and alternatives
Issue superseding scenario versions with a change reason when an input changes
May not assign final affected status or claim status without an assessor mandate

roles.name: Impact assessor
responsibilities: Assign per-member status with justification and determination time, including negative, unknown, conditional and non-propagating outcomes
Characterise effect kind, polarity, magnitude, ordering and declared accumulation
Assign claim status and likelihood or confidence qualifiers on the bound scales
Sign the limitation and uncertainty disclosure and take accountability for the release

roles.name: Reviewer and challenger
responsibilities: Re-execute traversal from the cited snapshot, profile and code-list versions and record whether the result reproduces
Challenge exclusions, completeness codes and any attributed-cause claim lacking cited evidence
Record a reproduction failure as an auditable finding and mark the result unverifiable where citations do not resolve
Cannot alter a released record; may only request supersession

roles.name: Dependency data owner (external to this split area)
responsibilities: Own dependency edges, edge typing, criticality and graph snapshots consumed here
Receive and triage data-quality findings raised by impact analysis without those findings constituting edits
Publish immutable, hashed snapshots with snapshot times so that results are reproducible

roles.name: Change or risk decision owner (external)
responsibilities: Consume qualified results to authorise, defer, reject or accept risk
Hold sole authority to act on an impact result, including any decision to notify or to remediate
Record the decision in the change or risk model, citing the exact result version relied on

roles.name: Retention and privacy policy owner (external)
responsibilities: Set retention periods, legal hold and disposition schedules for impact records
Adjudicate erasure requests and authorise redaction in narrative fields
Execute destruction where required, since this model performs none

access.default_rule: Read access to an impact record requires authorisation for every entity referenced in its affected set. Where that is impracticable, a redacted projection is served that preserves member counts by status, the traversal completeness code, the claim statuses and the full limitation disclosure while withholding entity identifiers, paths and exclusion detail. No principal receives a result without its claim status, completeness code and non-authorisation statement. Write access is scoped by role to the artifact type that role owns, and no read grant ever implies a right to act on the result.
exceptions: Security-sensitive scenarios, such as an unremediated vulnerability path, may restrict path and exclusion detail to a narrow audience while still publishing the per-member status with its justification - mirroring the practice of publishing an exploitability status and justification without exploitation detail.

Supervisory or regulatory recipients may be entitled to unredacted access to the dependency register and the impact analyses derived from it; that entitlement is defined by the applicable regulation and the adopting Dimension, not granted by this model.

Draft scenarios, draft results and unsigned disclosures are visible only to the scenario author, the assigned assessor and the steward, and must never be cited by a downstream decision; a citation of a draft is a conformance failure.

Emergency read during an ongoing disruption may be granted at artifact scope for a bounded period. The grant is recorded as an access exception with an expiry and a justification; the record content itself is unchanged and no write right is conferred.

Where an affected-set member belongs to a third party under a confidentiality obligation, that member may be served as an anonymised placeholder that retains its status, justification and path length but not its identity, with the substitution disclosed in the completeness section.
audit_requirements: Every release, supersession, withdrawal, status change, redaction and access exception is emitted as an audit payload carrying actor, role, action, artifact identifier and version, and time in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset. This model supplies the payload and never stores, retains, orders, protects or adjudicates the audit trail, which is owned by the referenced audit model.

A released result must be reproducible from its cited snapshot, propagation profile and code-list versions. A reproduction failure is itself a recordable finding, and the affected result is marked unverifiable rather than quietly re-derived.
Redaction records retain a hash of the pre-redaction canonical form so that suppression of members, paths or disclosure text is detectable without exposing the redacted content.
Filtered and redacted reads record the counts they suppressed, so that later review can establish what a decision-maker was and was not shown at the time.

required_fields: Split-area boundary statement (impact-scenario area versus dependency-assertion area)
Dependency-graph snapshot source and hashing convention
External alignment bindings with versions (PROV, OWL-Time, CSAF, VEX, RFC 3339)
read_order: AGENTS.md first: resolve Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any read or write, and stop if any is missing.
Specification URL: read the scope, out-of-scope list and boundary notes, so that no agent attempts approval, execution, notification, enforcement or audit-trail writes from an impact context.
Split-area boundary statement: confirm that dependency edges, edge typing and graph snapshots are read-only inputs here before planning any traversal.

Storage type URL: identify the projection in use - document store, graph store, files under version control, or MCP-served resources - and confirm that the canonical form is projection-neutral and unchanged by it.
Interface URL: learn the concrete read and write surface, the mandatory version-pinning behaviour, the redaction behaviour and the fields that a projection may never strip.

Processes URL: follow the scenario framing, derivation, status assignment, effect characterisation, qualification, disclosure, reconciliation and supersession procedures, including escalation to the change and risk decision owners.
Bound code lists and the current dependency-graph snapshot source with its hash, immediately before deriving any affected set; refuse to derive if either is unresolved.

coverage.claim: This is a deliberately bounded pass covering impact-scenario semantics for WM-XCT-037 only: trigger and scenario inputs, counterfactual baseline, analysis mode and horizon, propagation assumptions, affected-set membership with explicit negative and unknown statuses, effect characterisation, path traceability with exclusions, and epistemic qualification with mandatory limitation disclosure. Typed dependency-edge assertion, edge criticality and graph-snapshot maintenance are the adjacent split area and are deliberately absent, consumed here only by citation. The structure is grounded in statutory impact-assessment requirements for a baseline and effect typing, risk-assessment guidance on impact, likelihood, assumptions and confidence, vulnerability-exchange practice on explicit negative determinations, provenance vocabulary for derivation, and exposure-assessment practice separating exposure from effect. No conformance with any cited instrument is claimed, and no universal or metaphysical completeness is asserted.

checklist.notes: Scenario, baseline, propagation profile, affected-set register, trace record and disclosure each carry a stable identifier plus a separate monotonic version. Identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed registry identifier or IRI, then a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID, and explicitly forbids dates, titles, statuses and severities as identifiers.

Draft to released to superseded to withdrawn or tombstoned, with immutability on release, explicit supersession links and change reasons. The lifecycle of the analysed change or incident is not modelled here; only the assessment record's own lifecycle is.

Trigger-to-seed alteration links, seed-to-member paths, antecedent links for downstream effects, declared accumulation links, alternative-scenario links and supersession links. Dependency edges themselves are referenced by citation and never defined, typed or retracted here.

Trigger time, effect time, baseline observation time, analysis time and observation or ingestion time are separate fields; RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset is required and never defaulted. Horizons, bands, permanence and reversion time are declared; OWL-Time intervals and Allen relations are an optional alignment.

Every result cites its scenario version, graph snapshot with time and hash, baseline version, propagation profile version, code-list versions and accountable assessor, shaped to PROV Entity, Activity and Agent with qualified derivation. PROV influence is explicitly flagged as non-causal.

Steward, scenario author, assessor, reviewer, external dependency data owner, external decision owner and external retention and privacy owner are separated. Only the external decision owner may act on a result; entity ownership itself belongs to the registry.

Re-execution from cited snapshot, profile and code-list versions is the primary validation. Justification is mandatory for negative and non-propagating determinations, claim status is mandatory for every outcome, unrecognised codes must canonicalise to unknown, and unresolvable citations mark a result unverifiable rather than triggering silent re-derivation.

Default read is tied to entitlement over every referenced entity, with redacted projections that preserve counts, statuses and disclosures; scopes are bundle, layer, finding and artifact. Exceptions cover sensitive paths, supervisory recipients, drafts, bounded emergency reads and third-party anonymisation.

No default deletion; supersession, withdrawal and tombstones retain identity, version and reason. Retention periods, legal hold and destruction are set and executed by the adopting Dimension's retention policy owner and the trigger-owning model, explicitly outside this model's boundary. Cascading deletion from upstream registries is prohibited; redaction retains a pre-redaction hash.

Versioned bindings to PROV, OWL-Time, CSAF, VEX and RFC 3339, each recorded as an alignment with conflicts noted and no conformance claimed. The canonical form is projection-neutral, so document stores, graph stores, version control and MCP interfaces are projections rather than compatibility events.

Baseline kind, source, observation or projection time, effect expression mode and revision handling are mandatory, with none-declared as an explicit recorded value that forces a limitation note. Grounded in the statutory requirement for a baseline scenario and its likely evolution without the project, corroborated by the European Commission impact assessment method.

Likelihood and confidence qualifiers on Dimension-bound scales with the assigning agent recorded, plus a mandatory disclosure of forecasting method, difficulties, data deficiencies, unmodelled mechanisms and main uncertainties. No calibrated vocabulary is prescribed, which is stated rather than hidden.

Claim status separates exposure inference, modelled prediction, observed outcome and attributed cause. Traversal reachability may only yield exposure inference; attributed cause requires cited evidence and is downgraded otherwise. Prospective analysis, retrospective observation and reconciliation are distinct modes that never overwrite one another.

Excluded edges and nodes with reason codes and a traversal completeness code are mandatory on every trace record, and unreachable or unmodelled regions must be described. Absence from a result set is explicitly not equivalent to a negative determination.

Only a coarse organisational, contractual and geographic scope descriptor is carried. No source used in this pass fixes a geometry or spatial-reference representation for the extent of an effect, and transboundary effects are named in the environmental impact assessment source but not modelled here. Geometry should be delegated to a geospatial sibling model; treating the descriptor as a spatial model would be unsupported.

Effect and trigger magnitudes cite external scales and units, but no cited source supplies a cross-domain severity scale or band boundaries. Magnitude comparability across Dimensions, and across security, environmental and operational subjects, is therefore not guaranteed and is not claimed.

Sensitive-path restriction publishing status without exploitation detail, third-party anonymisation, redaction with retained hashes, and integrity attestation consumed from referenced audit and security models rather than implemented here.

known_omissions: Quantitative propagation computation: cascading-failure, queueing, network-reliability and percolation models. This pass records propagation assumptions, paths and exclusions but prescribes no algorithm and no attenuation function.
Probabilistic graph inference and correlated or common-cause failure structure beyond conditional predicates on individual steps.

Formal causal identification methods - potential outcomes, structural causal models, identification assumptions and confounding control. The model records claim status and evidence citations but supplies no causal inference method.
Monetary valuation, cost-benefit analysis, discounting and impact-weighted aggregation of effects.

Sector-specific severity scales, impact tolerances, recovery time and recovery point objectives, and criticality thresholds; these are left to the adopting Dimension and to the risk and continuity models.

Consultation and participation procedure. Statutory impact assessment regimes require consultation of affected parties and authorities; this model deliberately excludes who must be consulted and how, because that is procedural authority it does not hold.
Simulation, what-if execution, blast-radius visualisation and any interactive analysis tooling.

Calibrated likelihood vocabulary. A calibrated confidence-and-likelihood guidance source could not be retrieved live in this pass, so no scale is prescribed and the Dimension must bind its own; this is recorded as an evidence gap rather than filled by assumption.
conflicts: The statutory vocabulary of indirect, secondary and cumulative effects is domain-causal, whereas indirect in dependency traversal means graph distance greater than one. The two do not coincide. This model requires the traversal basis to be declared explicitly and does not assert equivalence, so a result labelled indirect must not be read as satisfying a statutory indirect-effect requirement.

NIST SP 800-30 frames impact as adverse harm arising from a threat event, while change-impact analysis must also represent neutral and beneficial effects. The polarity field departs from that framing deliberately; consumers mapping to a NIST-style risk model will find positive-polarity effects have no target.

VEX and CSAF status justifications are vulnerability- and code-path-specific, for example vulnerable code not in execute path. They map only partially onto general non-propagating dependency reasons, so the alignment is an explicitly partial mapping and not a conformance claim; a general non-propagation reason has no VEX equivalent and vice versa.

PROV-O's wasInfluencedBy is intentionally weaker than causation. Consumers that read PROV edges emitted by this model as causal claims will misread every exposure inference; the alignment therefore carries an explicit non-causal caveat.

CSAF permits both integer and semantic document versions and uses release dates prominently in tracking. This model is stricter: versions are monotonic and never encode a date, and dates are never identity. Records exchanged with CSAF-shaped systems require a mapping note.

Statutory impact assessment expects a described set of reasonable alternatives evaluated within one assessment, whereas this model represents alternatives as sibling scenario versions linked by comparator role. This is a structural divergence that must be reconciled at export time.

IFRS S2 requires short, medium and long term horizons but does not fix their boundaries, and the environmental impact assessment regime uses the same terms with different implied durations. Horizon bands are therefore Dimension-declared and are not comparable across Dimensions without an explicit mapping.
regional_assumptions: Directive 2011/92/EU as amended, the European Commission Better Regulation Guidelines and Toolbox, and Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 are European Union instruments. They are used here as evidence that baseline scenarios, direct and indirect effect typing, scenario-based business impact analysis and maintained dependency registers are required somewhere in authoritative practice - not as obligations binding any adopting Dimension.
NIST SP 800-30 Revision 1 and the CISA VEX minimum requirements are United States federal guidance and are not binding outside that context; their vocabularies are borrowed, not imposed.
IFRS S2 applies only where a jurisdiction has adopted ISSB standards, and adoption varies; horizon banding is therefore left entirely to the adopting Dimension.

No assumption is made about a governing legal system, official language, calendar system or working-time convention. Horizon bands, severity scales, retention periods and evidence thresholds for attributed-cause claims are all Dimension-local parameters that this model requires to be declared but does not set.

The model assumes no particular sector. Where a Dimension operates under a sector regime that prescribes impact tolerances or notification duties, those requirements are satisfied in the risk, continuity and notification models, not here.
adversarial_checks: Can any bundle, layer, finding or function approve, authorise, schedule, execute or roll back a change? Checked against all eight functions and all nine findings: no. Approval and execution appear only as a required REFERENCE composition link to the change model, in out_of_scope, in a boundary note, and as a mandatory non-authorisation statement on every release.

Can anything here notify a party or produce a distribution list? No. Notification is a non-required REFERENCE link; the affected-set register is named as an input to notification and never as a notification, and no function has a send or dispatch effect.

Does anything claim causal certainty from dependency reachability? No. Claim status is a required data element, traversal reachability may only produce exposure-inference status, attributed cause requires cited evidence and is automatically downgraded without it, and the PROV alignment carries an explicit non-causal caveat.

Does any finding define, type, version, repair or retract a dependency edge, which belongs to the adjacent split area? No. Edges are consumed through a cited immutable snapshot; the propagation profile only selects and parameterises edge-type codes that already exist, and the derive function explicitly effects no change to the source graph.

Does the model own audit-trail, enforcement or evaluation-engine semantics? No. Audit requirements specify what payload must be emitted and explicitly disclaim capture, ordering, tamper-evidence, storage, retention, protection and replay; there is no enforcement, blocking or runtime evaluation function anywhere in the structure.

Could a negative or unknown result be hidden by omission? Blocked at three levels: canonicalisation may not drop entries and absence is not equivalent to not-affected; filtered and redacted reads must report suppressed counts by status; and draft patches removing a member require an exclusion reason code.

Is any identifier date-like, mutable or semantically overloaded? Checked across bundles, layers, findings, artifacts, functions, questions and data elements: all are lower-kebab-case, none contains a year, date or timestamp component, and the identity priority and serial naming rules explicitly bar dates, versions, titles, statuses and severities from serving as identity.

Could a reviewer falsify a published result? Yes by construction: snapshot, profile and code-list versions with hashes, every path, every exclusion with a reason, the completeness code and a deterministic canonical ordering are all published, and an unresolvable citation marks the result unverifiable rather than allowing silent re-derivation.

Does the model silently assume propagation is transitive or symmetric? No. Traversal direction, depth or stop conditions, non-propagating edge types, conditional predicates and cycle and multi-path handling must all be declared in a cited propagation profile before an affected set may be derived, and the derive function lists these as preconditions.

Does any finding populate both artifacts and an inline-only rationale, or neither? Checked on all nine: six declare exactly one artifact with a null rationale, and three - trigger input, analysis frame, and effect characterisation - declare an empty artifact array with a substantive rationale explaining that the content is a reference or a set of typed attributes on an artifact declared elsewhere.

Does the model become a master record for anything it does not own? No. Triggers, entities, edges, scales, units, audit entries and observations are all carried by reference with unresolvable-reference markers instead of local copies, and cascading deletion from upstream registries is prohibited precisely so that this model never repairs or reconstructs another model's state.
